extracted.intended_audience: citizens and state legislators (New York ratifying public); policymakers and readers evaluating the proposed U.S. Constitution
extracted.subtask_description: Analytical exposition of the powers conferred on the federal government and restrictions on state authority under the proposed U.S. Constitution, with explanations and practical examples of their necessity and limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform rule of naturalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorize the general government to establish a uniform rule of naturalization throughout the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: The dissimilarity of state naturalization rules creates intricate and delicate questions (e.g., free inhabitants vs. free citizens vs. people) and can allow an alien to evade disabilities by moving between states. A uniform federal rule prevents one state's law from being rendered paramount in another and avoids serious embarrassments (such as proscribed persons acquiring citizenship elsewhere).

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to establish uniform laws of bankruptcy
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish uniform laws of bankruptcy at the federal level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: Closely connected to commerce and prevents many frauds where parties or property lie or are removed into different States; expedient and unlikely to be questioned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prescribe proof and effect of public acts, records, and judicial proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Prescribe by general laws the manner in which the public acts, records and judicial proceedings of each State shall be proved, and the effect they shall have in other States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: An improvement on indeterminate Confederation clause; may be a convenient instrument of justice, particularly beneficial on borders where effects liable to justice may be translated suddenly into a foreign jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to establish post roads
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish post roads by federal authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: Harmless power that can, by judicious management, become productive of great public conveniency. Anything that facilitates intercourse between the States merits public care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote progress of science and useful arts (copyrights and patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Power 'to promote the progress of science and useful arts, by securing, for a limited time, to authors and inventors, the exclusive right to their respective writings and discoveries.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: Utility scarcely questioned; copyrights and patents align public good with individual claims. States cannot separately make effectual provisions; many have already anticipated congressional action by state laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive federal legislation over federal district and federal places
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercise exclusive legislation in all cases over such district (not exceeding ten miles square) as may become the seat of government, and over places purchased by consent of state legislatures for forts, magazines, arsenals, dockyards, and other needful buildings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: Necessity of complete authority at the seat of government to prevent insults, interruptions, dependence on the state for protection, and to preserve national independence; consent of the ceding State and protections for inhabitants (voice in elections, municipal legislature) address objections. Similar necessity for forts and other installations to protect public property and security.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration and punishment of treason with limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Power to declare the punishment of treason, with the stipulation that no attainder of treason shall work corruption of blood, or forfeiture, except during the life of the person attainted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: United States must be enabled to punish treason committed against it; convention wisely inserted definition and proof standards and restrained Congress from extending consequences of guilt beyond the person to avoid abuses of ‘artificial treasons.’

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission of new States with consent safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: Admit new States into the Union, with prohibitions: no new State formed within jurisdiction of any other State; no State formed by junction of two or more States or parts thereof without consent of legislatures of States concerned and of Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: Confederation omitted provisions; new system supplies precaution to avoid unilateral acts, to quiet jealousies of larger and smaller States, and to ensure concurrence of federal authority and concerned States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dispose of and regulate territory and property of the United States
rubrics_metrics.description: Dispose of and make all needful rules and regulations respecting the territory or other property belonging to the United States, with proviso that nothing shall prejudice any claims of the United States or of any particular State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: Power of great importance, required by reasons similar to other federal powers; the proviso is proper to address jealousies and claims (e.g., Western territory disputes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guarantee of republican form of government and protection for States
rubrics_metrics.description: Guarantee to every State a republican form of government; protect each against invasion; and, on application of the legislature or executive (when legislature cannot be convened), against domestic violence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale and limits: Federal government should defend republican institutions and protect weaker members against ambitious neighbors. Guarantee implies a remedy but does not permit substitution of antirepublican constitutions; federal interposition is limited to guaranteeing the continuation of a republican form as it exists or is legitimately changed. Protection against domestic violence is proper and historically grounded; federal interposition is meant to prevent or repress violence that local authority cannot handle, and ideally its existence will deter the need to use it. Examples and theoretical objections (majority vs. minority force) are addressed to justify the provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of pre-Constitution debts and engagements
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider all debts contracted, and engagements entered into, before the adoption of this Constitution, as being no less valid against the United States under this Constitution than under the Confederation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: Declaratory provision likely to reassure foreign creditors and to assert that moral obligations survive change in political form; omission to assert validity in favor of the United States need not be read as hostile because engagements are reciprocal and declaratory effect for one side implies the other.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment process with three-fourths ratification and two exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide for amendments to be ratified by three fourths of the States under two exceptions only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: Necessary to allow useful alterations suggested by experience; balances against extreme facility (too mutable) and extreme difficulty (perpetuating faults). Exceptions (including equality of suffrage in the Senate) protect residuary sovereignty of the States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ratification by nine States sufficient for establishment among ratifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: The ratification of the conventions of nine States shall be sufficient for the establishment of this Constitution between the States ratifying the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: Requiring unanimity would subject essential interests to caprice or corruption of a single member. Addresses delicate questions: (1) principle on which Confederation can be superseded without unanimous consent (self-preservation, breaches of compact); (2) relation between ratifying and nonratifying States (no political relation but moral relations and obligations remain; moderation and prudence urged).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibitions on State powers (treaties, coinage, paper money, attainder, ex post facto, impairing contracts, titles of nobility, letters of marque)
rubrics_metrics.description: No State shall enter into any treaty, alliance, or confederation; grant letters of marque and reprisal; coin money; emit bills of credit; make anything but gold and silver a legal tender in payment of debts; pass any bill of attainder, ex post facto law, or law impairing the obligation of contracts; or grant any title of nobility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: Prohibitions copied or extended from Confederation; uniformity in foreign relations and currency is necessary; paper money and state-issued currencies have produced pestilent effects on confidence, industry, morals, and public character. Bills of attainder, ex post facto laws, and laws impairing contracts violate fundamental social compact; prohibition for personal security and private rights. Titles of nobility prohibition copied from Confederation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restraints on State regulation of imports/exports, tonnage, and military/foreign agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: No State shall, without the consent of Congress, lay any imposts or duties on imports or exports (except as absolutely necessary for executing inspection laws), and the net produce shall be for use of U.S. treasury; all such laws subject to revision and control of Congress. No State shall, without the consent of Congress, lay any duty on tonnage, keep troops or ships of war in time of peace, enter into any agreement or compact with another State or foreign power, or engage in war unless actually invaded or in imminent danger.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: Restraints enforce necessity of submitting regulation of trade to federal councils while allowing reasonable state discretion for inspection convenience; provides federal check against abuse. Other particulars (tonnage duties, troops, compacts, war) are self-evident or have been previously developed in reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessary and Proper Clause (laws to carry into execution constitutional powers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Power to make all laws which shall be necessary and proper for carrying into execution the foregoing powers, and all other powers vested by this Constitution in the government of the United States, or in any department or officer thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defense and limits: Without the substance of this power the Constitution would be a dead letter. Alternative formulations (prohibiting anything not expressly delegated; attempting to enumerate particular means; negative enumeration of exceptions; silence) are impractical. Remedies for misconstruction include checks by executive and judiciary and ultimate redress by the people via elections; federal usurpations may be more readily detected and redressed because State legislatures will notice invasions of their rights.
